_comment: mcp-servers.json — MCP wiring for labs-repo (course master copy).
What:   declares the two MCP servers that ship INSIDE this repo:
(a) bosch-canlog  — the Session 3 'corporate' FastMCP server
(mcp/mcp_server.py): CAN-log resources + parse tools, token
auth, audit logging;
(b) mock-analyzer — the Session 5/7 mock static analyzer
(mcp/mock-analyzer/server.py; course stand-in for the
qualified analyzer).
Both run from a repo-relative path — no install step, no network.
Used by: Session 3 (Lab 3-B wires bosch-canlog) and Session 5 (the
remediation loop queries mock-analyzer). .vscode/mcp.json is the
VS Code-format twin of this file and is what VS Code actually
reads; keep the two in sync.
Adjust: paths below are relative to the repo root (${workspaceFolder}).
If you relocate a server, update BOTH this file and
.vscode/mcp.json. For the cloud coding agent, register the same
servers under repo Settings > Copilot > coding agent > MCP.
Run:    requires the org policy 'MCP servers in Copilot' to be ENABLED
(ships disabled by default — see LIVE.md).
Note:   no secrets in this file, ever. Tokens arrive via environment or
VS Code 'inputs' prompts (secret storage) — see
docs/secrets-setup.md. Training servers accept any placeholder.
JSON has no comments — remove this _comment key in working copies.
Python: server commands use 'python' (not python3) so they work on Windows/Git Bash;
on Linux/macOS 'python' must resolve to Python 3 (Ubuntu: sudo apt install python-is-python3).

inputs.description: Bosch MCP service token (training: any placeholder, see docs/secrets-setup.md)
Mock analyzer service token (training: any placeholder — never commit a real secret)
